kyoto_isshisoden_nakamura.notes: [Kaiseki · Oike, two hundred years of Kyoto ryori] Behind a white noren on Tomikoji-dori, a house that began in 1827 when the first master carried Wakasa fish along the 鯖街道 (the mackerel road) to the palace and court nobles. Sixth-generation 中村元計 (Motokazu Nakamura) — once a Zen trainee at 天龍寺 and now a doctor of food science — keeps the two dishes passed from father to son: sake-grilled guji, finished as a soup with hot water over the bones, and a white-miso zoni made without dashi. Courses are served in quiet private rooms over a courtyard; reviewers note three Michelin stars. Lunch around ¥20,000–30,000, dinner ¥40,000–50,000; book ahead; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site: founded in Bunsei 10 (1827) when the first master, 若狭屋清兵衛, carried Wakasa fish such as guji and mackerel to Kyoto for the palace and court nobles; the second generation began catering; the third, a tea devotee, made tea kaiseki catering the core; the fourth supplied the inns 柊家, 俵屋 and 炭家 during the war; after the war the restaurant opened on its present site, and the fifth generation built today's base. The sixth, 中村元計, studied at Tokyo University of Fisheries, trained as a Zen monk at 天龍寺 in 嵯峨嵐山, and in 2021 earned a doctorate in food and agricultural science at 龍谷大学, approaching cooking as science. Tabelog Award Bronze 2017–2023; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021. 2026 reviews call it Michelin three-starred.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「即味心也」 — taste is the heart: only a person's heart moves another's (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Sake-grilled guji; white-miso zoni.

kyoto_smart_coffee.vegan_detail: Ask. Black coffee suits; the pancakes, French toast, pudding and sandwiches use eggs, butter or dairy (2026 reviews).
kyoto_smart_coffee.hours_raw: 8:00–19:00 every day (Tabelog); the upstairs western-style lunch room keeps its own hours and is sometimes closed (October 2026). kyoto_smart_coffee.notes: [Kissaten · Teramachi, Kyoto's pancake kissaten since 1932] A wood-panelled, high-ceilinged coffee house in the Teramachi arcade, said to date from 1932, where the queue forms for the pancakes — crisp outside, soft inside, with butter and maple syrup — and the French toast. Pancake set ¥1,400; weekday afternoons have the shortest waits. Open daily 8:00–19:00; AMEX only.

kyoto_kissa_madrague.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: the menu is toast, sandwiches, spaghetti and curry; the famous egg sandwich comes on thick bread with demi-glace and mustard (official menu; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_kissa_madrague.vegan_detail: Ask. Food centres on eggs, ham, meat sauce and cheese, and the omelette is made with dashi; juices, tea and black coffee suit (official menu; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_kissa_madrague.hours_raw: 8:00–18:00 every day; last food order 17:00, drinks 17:30; closes early when food runs out; closed irregularly, with notices on Facebook (official site). Seats can be booked at the shop or by phone for 8:00 or 9:30 (morning) or 12:00 (lunch) (official site); lunch seats rotate hourly and walk-ins are possible, but booking is safer (Tabelog). Breakfast until 11:00 (October 2026). Only the Corona sandwich is sold to take away, ordered by phone two days ahead (official site). 18 seats; non-smoking (Tabelog). kyoto_kissa_madrague.notes: [Kissaten · Karasuma Oike, the Corona egg sandwich] A retro coffee house in a building that was Kissa Seven for about 50 years from 1963; after its master died in 2011, the son looked for someone to keep the shop going, and Madrague opened that September. About a year later the free paper 音読 asked the shop to carry on the famous egg sandwich of Corona, a western-style restaurant that had just closed, and Corona's master came to teach it in person. The result is a fist-sized, hot, dashi-soft omelette on bread with demi-glace and mustard (¥1,180) — cut it in half to eat. Breakfast sets until 11:00; book a seat for 8:00, 9:30 or 12:00. Open daily 8:00–18:00 (irregular closures); cash only.

roles: Owner (unnamed on the official site), who opened the shop with the owner’s wife
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: before opening, the owner managed a café tied to the revival of Kyoto townhouses and old shopping streets and wanted to get back to hands-on work; while looking for a property with the owner’s wife, the couple met the son of the master of Kissa Seven (in business from 1963 for about 50 years; the master died in 2011) and opened Kissa Madrague there in September 2011. The name is that of Brigitte Bardot’s villa in Saint-Tropez; the owner’s wife loved the actress. The owner once worked part-time at Francois, near Corona, and often ate Corona’s egg sandwich on breaks. The site also describes a team, 京都喫茶文化遺産, formed to take over and keep old neighbourhood kissaten. Tabelog Kissaten "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2022, 2026.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: to keep "the long-running neighbourhood kissaten with tradition", not a retro-styled café, and hand it on to the next generation.
chef_bio.specialty: Corona egg sandwich; Set A breakfast.

anecdotes.text: Per the official site: after customers said the old Corona sandwich had been softer or bigger, the owner reworked the bread, eggs, seasoning, cooking time and heat, the hand pressure when sandwiching and the cut, keeping the basics.

kyoto_akagakiya.gf_detail: Ask. A traditional izakaya: duck with a soy-based sauce, oden in broth (with fish cakes), tempura and sashimi with soy sauce; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
kyoto_akagakiya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: oden in broth, duck, fish and yakitori make up most of the menu (2026 reviews).
kyoto_akagakiya.hours_raw: 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:30), Monday to Saturday; closed Sunday and on Mondays that are public holidays (Tabelog). A queue forms from about 16:30; the owner hangs the noren at 17:00 and the first round is seated in arrival order (October–November 2026). Table seats can be booked, for 17:00 or 19:00 starts; the 11 counter seats are walk-in only (Tabelog; November 2026); same-day booking is hard (September 2026). Two-hour limit (October 2026). Menu without prices; bills around ¥4,000–6,000 a head (2026 reviews). 41 seats (11 counter, 30 on tatami); smoking allowed; cash only (Tabelog). 5 min walk from Sanjo Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_akagakiya.notes: [Izakaya · Kawabata Nijo, a 1930s tavern by the Kamo River] An old izakaya beside the Kamo River, with lantern light, a counter worn smooth and darkened beams; a reviewer gives its founding as 1934 and the move here as 1949. The line forms from 16:30 and the owner hangs the noren at 17:00. Almost every table orders the duck roast; the shime saba, kumiage yuba and Kyoto-style oden (the octopus takes time — order it early) are the other classics. The menu shows no prices, yet bills run around ¥4,000–6,000. Book a table for 17:00 or 19:00; the 11 counter seats are first come. Cash only; smoking allowed; closed Sunday.

kyoto_zen_cafe_kagizen.vegan_detail: Ask. Kudzu sweets, zenzai and seasonal wagashi are based on starch, beans, sugar and chestnut, but no ingredient list is published; the fruit sandwiches use cream (2026 reviews).

No reservations (Tabelog): take a number at the ticket machine; a queue can form before 11:00 and at busy times (September–October 2026). The fruit sandwiches can sell out by about 11:45 (September 2026). Payment is asked for 30 minutes before closing (October 2026). 16 seats (10 at tables, 6 at the counter); non-smoking; cards and QR payments (Tabelog). kyoto_zen_cafe_kagizen.notes: [Wagashi café · Gion, Kagizen's quiet café] The café that the old Gion wagashi house Kagizen Yoshifusa opened in 2012 down a back street opposite its ZENBI museum: dim, modern and calm, with a counter and a sofa. Order kuzumochi (¥1,200), the shop's kuzukiri with black syrup, or the seasonal jo-namagashi — chestnut kinton in autumn — with sencha, or come early for the fruit sandwiches, which can be gone before noon. Take a number at the machine; no bookings. One October 2026 visitor found the prices high for Gion and was asked to pay 30 minutes before closing. 11:00–18:00, closed Monday.

roles: Café of Kagizen Yoshifusa; no person is named in the sources
chef_bio.background: Per the Kagizen official site (read for batch 15): the company also runs ZEN CAFE and the ZENBI art museum. Per a 2026 review, a café opened in 2012 by Kagizen Yoshifusa, in business since the Kyōhō era, with modern ceramics by contemporary artists; opened 8 November 2012 (Tabelog). chef_bio.specialty: Kuzumochi; seasonal jo-namagashi; fruit sandwiches.

anecdotes.text: "The kuzumochi was so delicious that I could eat it on its own" — February 2026.
"Be careful, as the fruit sandwiches seemed to sell out by 11:45." — September 2026.

Second floor, up an outside staircase (October 2024). 2 min walk from Kyoto-Kawaramachi Stn (Hankyu) (Tabelog).
kyoto_ygrec.notes: [Curry · Shijo Kiyamachi, a couple's upstairs curry room] A retro curry shop up an outside staircase on the second floor of an old building by the river, run by a couple, with big windows. There are three curries — vegetable, beef and small shrimp — in a smooth, mild European-style sauce whose spice comes through late; the vegetable curry (¥1,400) is the one to order, heaped with about ten kinds of seasonal vegetables cooked several ways. Not fast, but the water is refilled and you are seen off warmly. No reservations; 11:30–14:00 and 16:30–23:00, closed Monday.

roles: Owner couple (unnamed in the sources)

kyoto_takasegawa_maki.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: the sea bream is eaten with the house-made dashi soy sauce (soy sauce is normally brewed with wheat), and the miso soup is made with Ehime barley miso (official site; Tabelog shop text; July 2026).
kyoto_takasegawa_maki.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the menu is built on raw sea bream, dashi and egg yolk; the courses add fish, abalone and shellfish (official site; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_takasegawa_maki.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–14:00, until the sea bream runs out; dinner 18:00–21:00; closed irregularly (official site; Tabelog). Courses, lunch or dinner, must be booked by 18:00 two days before (official site); the lunch course allows 1 hour 30 minutes (official site). Tabelog says reservations are taken for groups of 10 or more, yet also sets rules for lunch bookings, and 2026 reviewers booked lunch for one or two; a May 2026 weekday walk-in was seated at once. Over 10 minutes late and the table may go to those waiting (Tabelog). 14 seats (4 counter, 10 table); non-smoking; cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) accepted, no e-money or QR; children welcome (Tabelog). The restroom is outside (July 2026). 3 min walk from Kyoto-Kawaramachi Stn, 4 min from Gion-Shijo Stn (official site).
kyoto_takasegawa_maki.notes: [Tai-meshi · Kawaramachi, Uwajima's sea bream rice by the Takase River] A townhouse restaurant down a back street on the Takase River, past a small inner garden, where a couple from Uwajima in Ehime serve their home town's tai-meshi: thin slices of raw sea bream in the house dashi soy sauce, eaten first as sashimi, then over rice, then with an egg yolk on top. Lunch gozen from ¥2,200 (double sea bream ¥2,860), served until the fish runs out; the mikan juice is pressed from the okami's brother's Uwajima orchard. Courses (¥6,600 lunch, ¥16,500 dinner) need booking two days ahead. One August 2026 reviewer found the taste simple, like a basic egg over rice.

roles: Chef (the shop’s Tabelog text: "Enjoy the culinary world crafted by Chef Makino")
chef_bio.origin: Uwajima, Ehime (Tabelog shop text: "Tai Meshi from Uwajima, made by a chef from Uwajima"; official site: a couple from Uwajima runs the shop)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: "宇和島出身の夫婦が手掛ける" (run by a couple from Uwajima); the mikan juice is made only for Maki by the okami’s brother in Uwajima; the group has three shops in Kyoto (高瀬川 槇, 鯛めし槇 金閣寺店, 京都寺町 鯛めし槇) and one in Ehime (鯛めし槇 松山店); TV appearances include Kansai TV "よーいドン！" (June 2023) for this shop. The shop’s Tabelog text: a building with the feel of the Edo period and an inner garden, low-pesticide ingredients and few additives, Uwajima’s local cooking combined with past experience. Opened 23 June 2019 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the shop’s Tabelog text: "food" is made of "people" and "goodness", so the kitchen aims for dishes that are kind to the body.
chef_bio.specialty: Uwajima tai-meshi; tai-meshi courses with clay-pot rice.

anecdotes.text: "Upon entering and taking my seat, the owner greeted me by name, which was a lovely touch." The reviewer’s wife does not eat squid, and the course dish was changed to taro at the last minute. — November 2026.

"The sea bream is served until it runs out, so if you definitely want to try it, I recommend arriving early." The same reviewer found the flavour "quite simple, resembling a basic egg over rice". — August 2026.
"This rich mikan juice is freshly squeezed from the mikan orchard of the owner's brother in Uwajima City, Ehime Prefecture, and is not available for sale anywhere else." — July 2026.
"You can also add more for an extra JPY 660, so you can place an additional order during your meal." — March 2026.

kyoto_nihon_ryori_tokuo.gf_detail: Ask. Omakase courses of sashimi, dashi soups, soft-shelled turtle chawanmushi, Saikyo-miso grilled fish, tempura and breadcrumbed fries, with soy- and miso-based seasonings throughout; no gluten information (official site; 2026 reviews).

kyoto_nihon_ryori_tokuo.hours_raw: Lunch 12:00–14:00 (last entry 12:30), Wednesday to Saturday; dinner 18:00–22:00 (last entry 20:00), Tuesday to Saturday; no lunch on Tuesday; closed Sunday and Monday (official site; Tabelog). kyoto_nihon_ryori_tokuo.notes: [Kappo · Kiyamachi, Shinji Tokuo's counter] A Kiyamachi kappo by the Takase River, open since 2005, where Shinji Tokuo buys at the market each morning and cooks without show: "food you never tire of", in the shop's words. Sit at the polished zelkova counter for omakase courses — lunch ¥10,800, dinner ¥24,000, tax and service included — of sashimi, soft-shelled turtle chawanmushi, wasabi wagyu steak, homemade karasumi with daikon and Saikyo-miso fish; marunabe turtle hot pot is the house dish. Reviewers praise the warm welcome from the chef, the proprietress and the young staff. Tabelog Bronze 2017–2021. Lunch Wed–Sat, dinner Tue–Sat; book lunch a day ahead. One April 2026 reviewer wrote that the shop generally does not take bookings from inbound tourists.

roles: Owner-chef
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: 日本料理とくを marked its 21st anniversary on 11 February 2026; the staff page lists 徳尾 真次 (born 19 January, from Kyoto Prefecture, hobbies travel and playing in a band) and four more staff, from Fukuoka and Amami Ōshima (Kagoshima); "私も含め、スタッフも若い者ばかりです" (the owner and the staff are all young). An April 2026 regular describes the head chef as "sometimes a band member, sometimes a horse owner, and sometimes a loving traveler", says the shop has been run with the proprietress for over 20 years, and that it serves black soybeans and young Tsukahara bamboo shoots year after year. Tabelog Award Bronze 2017–2021; Tabelog Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: dishes that make the most of the ingredients bought every day, handled lightly — no showy effects, but food you never tire of; Japanese cuisine to be enjoyed more casually.
chef_bio.specialty: Marunabe (soft-shelled turtle hot pot); charcoal-grilled wagyu; karasumi daikon.

"The warm welcome from the head chef, the proprietress, and the staff creates a cozy, home-like atmosphere" — September 2026 (a 14th visit).

kyoto_torikago.notes: [Yakitori · Shijo Omiya, a one-cook charcoal counter] An eight-seat yakitori counter in a quiet street near Shijo-Omiya, opened in 2023 by Kato, who cooked at Kyoto's Torisaki before: skewers of Date chicken grilled over strong, direct charcoal heat in the Torishiki manner, eleven to a course with pickles, chicken soup, a rice bowl and dessert. ¥17,000 covers the food and all the drinks (¥15,000 with soft drinks). Kato grills and serves alone, and reviewers single out the warmth of the welcome; one July 2026 regular calls the gizzard "undoubtedly the best I've ever had". Two seatings, 17:00 and 20:30; reservations only, hard to get — watch Instagram for cancellations. Tabelog Yakitori WEST 100 2024, 2025.

roles: Owner-chef, who grills and serves alone (2026 reviews: "The owner, Mr. Kato")
chef_bio.background: Per 2026 reviews: Kato previously worked at Torisaki in Kyoto (February, May and September 2026), and the shop grills in the Torishiki style (February and May 2026). Another July 2026 reviewer has known the chef since the training days. Opened 20 August 2023 (Tabelog). Tabelog Yakitori WEST "Tabelog 100" 2024, 2025.
chef_bio.specialty: Charcoal-grilled skewers of Date chicken; gizzard.

"On the other hand, since Mr. Kato handles all the cooking himself, the variety of skewers and choices for finishing dishes are somewhat limited." — February 2026.

kyoto_kobayashi_saketen.notes: [Standing bar · Kawaramachi, a fridge of craft beer and gin] A modern take on the liquor shop that lets you drink on the premises, in the Kayukoji alley a few steps from Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn: choose a can or bottle from the refrigerated cases — craft beer, sake, wine, a strong line of Japanese craft gin — and drink at the standing counter outside or the seats inside; the owner brings the glass, printed with the shop emblem. roles: Owner (unnamed in the sources)

kyoto_sarasa_kayukoji.gf_detail: Ask. Lunch plates lean on fried food — kara-age, tonkatsu, chicken katsu with demi-glace — next to curry, dry curry, taco rice and cakes; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
kyoto_sarasa_kayukoji.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options and a focus on vegetables, but the reviewed plates are meat-based and the desserts use cream and cheese; no vegan menu is published (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_sarasa_kayukoji.hours_raw: 12:00–22:00, closed Wednesday (official site; Tabelog). Lunch 12:00–15:00, coffee only 15:00–18:00, dinner 18:00–22:00; last order food 21:00, drinks 21:30 (Tabelog). Bookings by phone only (Tabelog note of 29 May 2026); a queue can form at opening, so booking is advised (August, October 2026). 90-minute seating limit (August 2026 on a public holiday; October 2026). Orders by QR code (August 2026); water is self-service (August 2026). 60 seats over two floors (10 counter, 18 sofa, 32 table); non-smoking, with a smoking area in the ground-floor courtyard; cash only — no cards, e-money or QR payments (Tabelog). 1 min from Hankyu Kawaramachi Stn exit 6 (Tabelog).
kyoto_sarasa_kayukoji.notes: [Café · Kawaramachi, a two-floor townhouse café down an alley] Through a narrow entrance in the Kayukoji alley, a few steps from Kawaramachi Stn, the room opens into a surprisingly large old wooden house with heavy beams, retro counter seats downstairs, roomy table seating upstairs, and rows of manga on display. Lunch is generous plates at about ¥1,280–1,350 (kara-age, curry, taco rice), afternoons are coffee and house cakes, and at night it turns to drinks and small plates until 22:00. A line forms at noon, so phone ahead; seating is 90 minutes. Part of SARASA, a Kyoto café company dating from 1984; this shop opened in 2007. Cash only; closed Wednesday.

roles: Run by 株式会社サラサ (SARASA inc), representative director 尾崎 友哉 (official site); no kitchen staff are named
chef_bio.background: Per the official company page: SARASA opened in December 1984 on the first floor up of "wood inn", a converted kimono shop at Tominokoji Sanjo; a second shop followed at Nishijin in 2000 and サラサ3 in 2005; in October 2007 the main shop moved from Tominokoji Sanjo to Shinkyogoku Shijo-agaru and opened as this Kayukoji shop (Tabelog gives the opening as 6 November 2007). 尾崎 joined in 2008; a new company, 株式会社サラサ, took over the running in April 2026. The company now runs さらさ西陣 (in a former public bath), さらさ花遊小路, さらさ3, サラサケーキ工房 and CLAMP COFFEE. Tabelog's introduction says the name comes from sarasa, a fabric that spread from the Middle East along the Silk Road.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official company page: the thing the company values most is kindness (親切心) toward everyone it deals with, from staff and suppliers to local customers and visitors to Kyoto.
chef_bio.specialty: Lunch plates; house-made cakes; coffee.

anecdotes.text: "The meal included kara-age and tonkatsu with a sweet sauce. Since it gets busy, I recommend making a reservation." — August 2026.

"I arrived a few minutes before opening, and there was already a line, but I managed to get in during the first round." — October 2026.

kyoto_maison_de_frouge.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: the range is shortcake, mille-feuille, tarts, roll cake, financiers and madeleines; no gluten-free item is listed (official site; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_maison_de_frouge.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the cakes are built on whipped cream, eggs, butter and cheese (shortcake, pudding, cheesecake, mousse) (official site; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_maison_de_frouge.hours_raw: 11:00–17:00 every day, open all year (Tabelog). No reservations for the café or for holding cakes; pay first when buying in the shop; phone orders need a bank transfer in advance (Tabelog). 9 seats; the eat-in seats can be full (October 2026). Non-smoking; credit cards accepted, no e-money or QR payments (Tabelog). Children welcome (Tabelog). 3 min walk from Karasuma Oike Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_maison_de_frouge.notes: [Strawberry sweets · Karasuma Oike, a strawberry-only patisserie] A small white-and-brown shop off Sanjo where every cake is a strawberry cake. Founder Mika Watabe was working in fashion design when a friend brought round some remarkably good strawberries; the visit to the grower behind them led to the first shop in 2003. Fully ripe berries now come straight from farms around Japan, a different variety each day. The premium shortcake (about ¥1,450–1,595) layers strawberries inside and on top; the mille-feuille comes tied with a ribbon you snip with tiny scissors. Nine café seats, no bookings; 11:00–17:00 every day. Prices are high, as reviewers note.

roles: Founder (official site profile: Mika Watabe)
Representative director of 株式会社ミュウ, the operating company (official company page: 代表取締役 渡部美佳)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: while working in fashion planning and design, Watabe was so moved by strawberries a friend introduced that the shop for strawberry sweets opened in 2003; the farm that grew those berries became a contract grower, sending only berries ripened in the field. The site credits Watabe with more than 100 recipes across Japanese, Western and Chinese sweets, appearances on TV, in magazines and at events, and work as an adviser on strawberry breeding for agricultural research bodies. Company history: opened in April 2003 on Senbon-dori in Kamigyo-ku; moved to Sanjo, Nakagyo-ku, in March 2014 (Tabelog: 9 March 2014); the company was set up in March 2013, has a strawberry laboratory and production atelier in Okayama Prefecture, and lists 株式会社三越伊勢丹, 株式会社大丸松坂屋百貨店, 株式会社高島屋 and 株式会社阪急阪神百貨店 as trading partners. Tabelog Sweets WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023 and 2026.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: to change how strawberries are distributed in Japan — avoiding the early picking used for market looks, buying fully ripe berries from farms each time, and simplifying packing so growers spend less — so that customers can taste truly good strawberries.
chef_bio.specialty: Premium strawberry shortcake; strawberry mille-feuille.

anecdotes.text: A September 2026 visitor noted that, ten days earlier, the shortcake had been ranked first in its category in a poll of 10,000 Kansai residents on the TV show "Chachai-re Monday"; even the restroom had strawberry decorations.
"You cut the ribbon with the adorable little scissors provided." — the strawberry mille-feuille, made with strawberries from Shiga, October 2026.

An October 2026 reviewer described the shortcake as four layers of strawberries between the sponge, and the strawberry trifle as made from the cake trimmings left from other cakes, at a much lower price.
A September 2026 visitor passed over the shortcake at over ¥1,500 and had the limited strawberry-caramel and lemon-cream pudding (¥780) with wild berry tea instead.

kyoto_common_one_bar.gf_detail: Ask. A cocktail and whisky bar; beer-based drinks such as the Red Eye contain gluten, and no gluten information is published (official site; 2026 reviews).

Cover charge ¥1,100 per person; the private rooms are by reservation at ¥1,700 per person (official site). Reservations taken (Tabelog). 25 seats: a counter, sofas and tatami private rooms for 4 and 6; smoking allowed; JCB, AMEX and Diners cards, no e-money or QR payments (Tabelog). Opened 23 August 2010 (Tabelog). About 5 min walk from Gion-Shijo or Sanjo Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_common_one_bar.notes: [Bar · Gion Shinbashi, a hidden machiya cocktail bar] Off a stone-paved Gion lane by the Shirakawa, a dark gate you might not take for an entrance leads down a lit stone path to a century-old townhouse: tatami private rooms along the corridor, then a high-ceilinged room with a one-slab counter facing a glowing back bar and an illuminated garden. Seasonal fresh-fruit cocktails and well-made classics (Martini, Rob Roy), plenty of single malt, and non-alcoholic or lighter drinks on request. Cover ¥1,100; two drinks with cover ¥4,700 in May 2026. Open nightly 18:00–02:00. A sister bar of Gion's FINLANDIA BAR.

roles: Run by 株式会社ケイ・ステージ (K-stage), representative 世古昌弘 (official company page); a July 2026 review calls it one of five establishments run by bartender Seko
chef_bio.background: Per the official company page: K-stage took over ぎをん FINLANDIA BAR (opened 1982 as the sister of a Finnish restaurant, FINLANDIA, from 1976) in 2002; in August 2010 it opened 何生館, a base for Japanese culture in a Gion Shinbashi townhouse more than 100 years old that belonged to a relative of one of the managers, and The Common One Bar Kyoto inside it. Sister venues: The Northern Lights Corner on Kayukoji (2013), Turquoise Bar at Kiyamachi Shijo (2016 as TurQuois Bar 2), and CLASSIC TEA & COCKTAILS ぎをん新橋 何生庵 in the same building (2021). A related company, アルコ・ノルディック株式会社 (2023), imports a Finnish vodka (コスケンコルヴァ). Tabelog Bar "Tabelog 100" 2022.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal fresh-fruit cocktails; classic cocktails; single malt.

anecdotes.text: "You enter through a dark gate that you might not even realize is the entrance, and as you follow the lights on the stone path, you arrive at a bar that feels like a grand residence." — May 2026.
A February 2026 group booked a private tatami room; the bar prepared non-alcoholic cocktails for the members who do not drink.
A July 2026 reviewer, celebrating an 80th birthday in a tatami room, watched the 80-year-old and a 79-year-old enjoy shots.
A June 2026 regular notes there was a period when the customers were mostly visitors from abroad, and that the crowd has recently become more mixed.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (k-stage.jp): ザ・コモン・ワン・バー・キョウト、白川の石畳から路地を入った別世界、一枚板のカウンター、季節のフルーツのカクテル、ウイスキー、ワイン、チャージ1,100円、個室は予約制で1,700円、18:00〜02:00 (L.o. 01:30)、東山区新橋通大和大路東入元吉町46番地 何生館内。会社概要: 株式会社ケイ・ステージ、代表者 世古昌弘、2002年 ぎをん FINLANDIA BAR の経営権を引き継ぐ、2010年8月 祇園白川に築百年以上の町屋を改装した何生館を開館し同時にバーを開業、2013年 The Northern Lights Corner、2016年 TurQuois Bar 2 (のち Turquoise Bar)、2021年 何生庵、2023年 アルコ・ノルディック設立 (コスケンコルヴァ・ウォッカの輸入)。食べログ: バー、25席、個室 (4人・6人)、喫煙可、カード (JCB・AMEX・Diners)、2010年8月23日オープン、ぎをん FINLANDIA BAR の姉妹店、バー百名店 2022。口コミ (2026年、英語): 季節のフルーツのカクテル、マティーニ、ロブロイ、シングルモルト、ノンアルコールのカクテル、2杯とチャージで4,700円 (2026年5月)。

kyoto_hyssop.gf_detail: Ask, and tell the restaurant in advance: it asks guests with allergies to say so beforehand and warns that, depending on the allergy, it may not be able to adapt on the day (Tabelog). Lunch sets include bread or rice, fritters, miso sauces and wontons; dinner has pasta (official menu; 2025–26 reviews).
kyoto_hyssop.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options and the cooking is built on vegetables, with a shojin (vegetarian) dashi in some soups, but most sets carry chicken, pork, fish or egg; one spring 2025 lunch let the diner pick the wonton filling (2025–26 reviews).
kyoto_hyssop.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–15:00 (last order), closing 16:00; dinner 17:30–21:00 (last order), closing 22:00; closed days follow the building (official site). Tabelog gives the same two sittings (lunch last orders food 15:00, drinks 15:30; dinner food 21:00, drinks 21:30) and in its notes a continuous 11:30–22:00 day with lunch last order 14:30, brunch and desserts until 16:30 and no café service during lunch; closed irregularly. Bookings online (TableCheck link on the official site; Tabelog); party plans for 10 or more by phone (Tabelog). 54 seats at 2- and 4-person tables, sofa seats and an open terrace; a table charge applies on the terrace (Tabelog). Non-smoking; cards and PayPay; wheelchair accessible (Tabelog). The bill could not be split per person for a group of five (October 2026). 4th floor of GOOD NATURE STATION, 2 min walk from Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn (official site; Tabelog).
kyoto_hyssop.notes: [Vegetable-led restaurant · Shijo Kawaramachi, a greenhouse room four floors up] The restaurant of GOOD NATURE STATION, next to Takashimaya: a room full of plants with an open-atrium terrace, cooking mostly Kyoto-grown vegetables simply. Lunch is a seasonal set with a medicinal-food theme — five small deli dishes, soup, a main of Tanba chicken or Kyoto pork, multigrain rice and a small dessert (¥2,500–3,400 in 2026); dinner turns to wine with caprese, duck-ragù pasta, venison and Kameoka beef. Terrace seats carry a table charge, and a September 2026 diner on the open terrace worried about the many birds overhead. Book online; 11:30–16:00 and 17:30–22:00.

roles: Hotel restaurant; no chef or manager is named in the sources
chef_bio.background: Opened 9 December 2019 (Tabelog) on the 4th floor of GOOD NATURE STATION, the building of GOOD NATURE HOTEL KYOTO (official site; 2026 reviews). A July 2026 reviewer describes it as part of the Keihan group. Lunch sets change with the seasons; a repeat diner who visited from 2022 to October 2026 described the winter set as a way to experience "Winter Nourishment" through food and the lunch sets as medicinal-herb sets, and a July 2022 visit found an afternoon-tea wellness set themed on "Yaku Shoku Dougen" (the synergy of medicine and food).
chef_bio.philosophy: Per Tabelog (the restaurant’s own text): ingredients, mainly vegetables, are sourced from local producers in Kyoto and cooked simply to bring out their character; the lunch course pairs "sauces that embody the essence of French cuisine" with Kyoto and Japanese flavours.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal vegetable lunch sets; Kameoka beef and venison at dinner.

anecdotes.text: "The interior is filled with greenery, making it feel like a botanical garden, and the open terrace seating is delightful." — September 2026.

kyoto_la_voiture.notes: [Tarte tatin café · Okazaki, half a century of tarte tatin] A small, old-fashioned café near Heian Shrine devoted to tarte tatin. Its story starts with the café 紅屋 that Yuri Matsunaga and husband 辰夫 opened in Gion in 1959; it became an art gallery, moved here in 1971 as a French restaurant beside the gallery, and turned into this café in 1987. Yuri kept baking the tarte tatin — honoured in France by the Confrérie des Lichonneux de tarte tatin in 2006 — until dying in 2014, and a grandchild bakes it now. About 20 apples go into each tart; pick from the day's varieties (Fuji ¥950 in 2026) and eat it warm with yogurt. No bookings; Tuesday–Sunday 11:30–18:00.

roles: Granddaughter of the founder, named in a January 2016 article as carrying on the recipe; the official site says the recipe is now baked by the founder’s grandchild
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: the first owners, 松永ユリ (Yuri Matsunaga in Leaf Kyoto and Fashion Headline) and 辰夫, opened the café 紅屋, forerunner of LA VOITURE, in Gion in 1959; out of a love of art it became the gallery 紅 in 1964; in 1971 the business moved to Okazaki, where the French restaurant LA VOITURE opened alongside the gallery. Yuri, captivated by the tarte tatin served as a French dessert, kept baking it and was admitted in France to the Confrérie des Lichonneux de tarte tatin in 2006. The official site gives Yuri’s death in 2014 at 96; a January 2016 Fashion Headline article says Yuri died "two years ago at the age of 92", was born in the Taisho era, always sat in a corner of the shop, and created the recipe after eating tarte tatin on a trip to France. Leaf Kyoto (March 2021) adds that the daughter, Tomomi, helped open the 1971 restaurant and that the shop became a tarte tatin café in 1987. The maker on the online shop is the company 株式会社 紅 at the shop address. Tabelog Sweets WEST "Tabelog 100" 2020, 2022, 2023, 2026.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: Yuri baked the tarte tatin "with an artist’s feeling", and that feeling and the recipe are being carried on by the grandchild.
chef_bio.specialty: Tarte tatin by apple variety; walnut caramel tart.

anecdotes.text: A September 2026 visitor learned that the classic Fuji tarte tatin is offered all year, alongside several seasonal varieties made with other apples.
"The cake was served slightly warm with yogurt on the side." — September 2026.

An October 2026 reviewer found one young staff member a little aloof; another that month said the staff were very kind and explained a lot.

kyoto_nikolabo.notes: [Italian · Shijo Kawaramachi, stews made for wine] A second-floor wine bistro on Kawaramachi-dori that calls itself a research lab for stews to go with wine. The chef — a sommelier from Kyotango — brings in fish and vegetables from that coast, and the menu lists more than 30 stews: braised pork belly tender enough for chopsticks with a lotus-root or apple sauce, lamb in tomato, coq au vin, tripe. Start with the carpaccio of the day or the water eggplant with parmesan. Reviewers in 2026 found the owner running the room alone, cooking, taking orders and the bill, so order starters and mains together. Dinner daily except Monday (from 17:00 at weekends); lunch on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday by booking only.

kyoto_otowa_sushi.gf_detail: Ask. Kyoto-style sushi: the inari skins are soaked in broth, the anago is grilled and the shiitake simmered sweet and savoury; no gluten information is published (2025–26 reviews).
kyoto_otowa_sushi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: mackerel, conger eel, egg and shrimp run through the menu, and the inari skins are soaked in broth (2025–26 reviews).
kyoto_otowa_sushi.hours_raw: 11:00–20:00 (last order 19:45), Tuesday to Sunday; closed Monday; hours may change (Tabelog). No reservations (Tabelog). Mushi-zushi (steamed sushi) is a winter dish: roughly October to March by a February 2026 blog, served into early April in the cold spring of 2025, and not served in summer (August 2026); in summer the speciality is hamo box sushi (February 2026). 20 seats; non-smoking; cards (VISA, AMEX, Diners), e-money and QR payments (Tabelog). kyoto_otowa_sushi.notes: [Sushi · Shinkyogoku, Kyoto's winter steamed sushi] An old Kyoto-sushi shop at the Shijo end of the Shinkyogoku arcade, dated to the Meiji era and said to be more than 120 years old. In winter a steamer at the door sends up clouds for the mushi-zushi: warm vinegared rice in a lidded Imari bowl, under shredded egg, with grilled anago and sweet-simmered shiitake (¥1,760, November 2025). Year round, reviewers praise the inari, with thick tofu skins soaked in broth, the saba-zushi and the small rolls; in summer, hamo box sushi. Single pieces can be ordered, and everything can be taken away. 11:00–20:00, closed Monday; no bookings.

roles: Owner (unnamed in the sources)
chef_bio.background: A Kyoto-sushi shop dated to the Meiji era: a March 2025 review says "established in the Meiji era", a January 2026 review "founded in the mid-Meiji period", and reviews from December 2025 and October 2026 give its age as 120 years and over 120 years. A February 2026 blog found no official site and notes that the shop is often introduced as founded in 1902 (Meiji 35); some articles present it as the birthplace of mushi-zushi. A January 2026 reviewer writes that the sushi rice is rested overnight to soften the vinegar before steaming.
chef_bio.specialty: Mushi-zushi (winter); inari-zushi; saba-zushi.

anecdotes.text: "In winter, there’s a large steamer in front of the restaurant, and passing by always makes me crave their steamed sushi." — February 2026.
"I was warned that it would be hot, and when I opened the lid, steam rose up" — March 2026.
An October 2026 diner who came in just before closing was given a ¥30 discount on a ¥550 mini maki, and called the owner "such a wonderful person".

A long-time regular wrote in June 2024 that a foreign visitor left after being shown a paper in English and that the shop might not be very welcoming to inbound customers; on the same regular’s April 2025 visit, a group of Western tourists was dining and the staff spoke English fluently.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 寿司、中京区新京極通四条上ル中之町565、阪急「河原町」駅から徒歩約5分、火〜日 11:00〜20:00 (L.O. 19:45)、月曜休み、予約不可、20席、禁煙、カード・電子マネー・QR 可、テイクアウト可、日本酒・焼酎。ブログ「日本全国食べ歩き」(2026年2月13日訪問): 京都の冬の名物の蒸し寿司を代表する老舗、公式サイトは見当たらない、明治35年 (1902年) 創業と紹介されることが多い、冬は蒸し寿司、夏は鱧の箱寿司、蒸し寿司はおおむね10〜3月、店頭にせいろ、京都河原町駅の9番出口のすぐ近く、むしすし1,600円 (税別)。口コミ (2024〜2026年、英語): 明治創業、120年以上、蒸し寿司 (錦糸玉子、穴子、椎茸、筍、かんぴょう)、いなり寿司840円、鯖寿司、京寿司 (箱・巻・鯖) 1,650円、Kyo no Shiki 2,100円、くらま、ミニ巻き寿司550円、かっぱ巻き・しんこ巻き、穴子きゅうり巻き1,600円、1個から注文可。

cultural_comfort.note: Order at the table or at the door for takeaway; check the display of samples by the entrance to see what each set holds; cards accepted.

kyoto_la_biographie.gf_detail: Ask when booking. Allergies are handled if told in advance, but not on the day (Tabelog); the omakase has included bread, a kumquat tart, a baba, and nama-fu (wheat gluten) in an amuse and a taiyaki (2024–25 reviews).
kyoto_la_biographie.vegan_detail: A vegetarian or vegan menu can be arranged — ask when booking; changes on the day are not possible (official site; Tabelog). The standard omakase uses beef, crab, fish, egg and cream.
kyoto_la_biographie.hours_raw: Lunch 12:00 (last entry) to 15:00, Friday to Sunday only; dinner 18:00 (last entry) to 22:00, Wednesday to Sunday; closed Monday and Tuesday and irregularly, with summer and New Year breaks posted on the official site (official site). Tabelog still lists lunch Wednesday to Sunday; the official site gives Friday to Sunday. Reservation only: by phone or online (TableCheck, OMAKASE, Ikkyu, linked from the official site); a booking with no word 10 minutes after the time is treated as cancelled (Tabelog). Omakase only: lunch ¥16,500 (8 dishes, about 2 hours), dinner ¥28,000 or ¥38,500 (11 dishes, about 2.5–3 hours), plus 10% service (official site). 8 counter seats facing the open kitchen; private hire up to 20; barrier-free, with gentle slopes throughout; non-smoking; cards, no e-money or QR (Tabelog; official site). 13 min walk from JR Nijo Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_la_biographie.notes: [French · Senbon, a Michelin-starred counter] Masahiro Takimoto was head chef at a Kyoto hotel from 1999, won a Michelin star in the guide's 2010 edition — the only French restaurant among Kyoto's starred Japanese kitchens, by the official profile — and opened La Biographie in 2011. Since 2021 it has been an eight-seat counter with an open kitchen on Shimodachiuri-dori, where the chef cooks and talks across the counter. The omakase begins with a five-taste aperitif and the signature egg, then Kasumi crab with senmaizuke and caviar, Kyoto mushrooms, and Kyoto Hime beef cooked slowly for about 100 minutes. Vegetarian or vegan menus can be arranged in advance. Lunch Friday–Sunday ¥16,500; dinner Wednesday–Sunday from ¥28,000, plus 10% service; booking only.

roles: Owner-chef (official site: chef profile and company founder; signs the shop notices); reviews from January 2025 and October 2026 describe the chef cooking behind the counter
chef_bio.background: Per the official profile: entered cooking as a pâtissier in 1982; trained at a hotel in Kyoto from 1983, then went to Europe; from 1987 trained at hotels and Michelin-starred restaurants in Switzerland and France; returned in 1992 and joined a Kyoto hotel, becoming head chef in 1999; won a star in the Michelin Guide 2010 edition (2009), the only French restaurant to do so in a Kyoto otherwise starred for Japanese cuisine; in 2011 founded 株式会社 T&T カンパニー and opened La Biographie...; selected for La Liste 1000 two years running from 2017; closed the 御池衣棚 shop in 2020 to move, and reopened at Shimodachiuri-dori Senbon in 2021 (Tabelog: 18 March 2021). A February 2024 review gives different years and names: part-time restaurant work from 17 as a pastry cook, the main dining room of the Kyoto Royal Hotel in 1984, Switzerland from 1987 ("International" and "Montre" in Zurich), an auberge in Albertville and "Alcazar" in Paris, back in Japan in 1990 at the Kyoto Brighton Hotel, head chef of its "Vi Za Vi" from 1996, own restaurant in 2011. A January 2025 review says the chef led the Brighton Hotel restaurant for 20 years. The official site reports that the restaurant kept its Michelin star in the 2026 Kyoto/Osaka guide. Tabelog French WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023 and 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: face each ingredient, judge it, and heat it without stress at the temperature that suits it, to draw out its nature; and a promise to the chef’s teacher, a great French chef, to pass the techniques, spirit and philosophy on to the next generation of Japanese cooks.
chef_bio.specialty: Aperitif of five tastes; the egg "microcosm"; low-temperature Kyoto Hime beef.

anecdotes.text: A February 2024 reviewer describes the signature egg as an homage to the "Oeuf à la Coque" of a three-star restaurant in Paris, and a July 2025 reviewer links the chef’s techniques to Alain Passard.
"Handcrafted right in front of us by the chef, who hand-cut the herbs into a bowl." — on the fresh herbal tea, October 2026.
A March 2026 lunch guest found the dishes delicate but the portions small, and the bill with wine, water and service steep for the value.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (la-biographie.info): 歴史ある平安宮中和院跡、下立売通千本に佇む本格フレンチレストラン、上京区田中町422-1 セントガーデン1F、シェフ 滝本 将博 (TAKIMOTO Masahiro)、1982年パティシエとして料理の世界に入る、1983年京都市内のホテルで修業後渡欧、1987年スイス・フランスのホテル、ミシュラン星付きレストランで修業、1992年帰国し京都市内ホテル入社、1999年料理長、2009年ミシュランガイド2010年版で星獲得 (日本料理ばかりの京都で唯一のフランス料理での星)、2011年株式会社 T&T カンパニー設立・La Biographie... 開業、2017年 La Liste 1000 に2年連続選出、2020年御池衣棚での営業を移転準備のため終了、2021年下立売通千本東入るに移転オープン、Michelin Guide 京都/大阪2026で星を維持。Lunch 16,500円 (金・土・日のみ、デザートを含む8皿、約2時間)、Dinner 28,000円・38,500円 (11皿、約2時間半〜3時間)、サービス料10%別、おまかせコースのみ、ベジタリアン・ヴィーガンのメニューも対応、バリアフリー、月曜・火曜定休・不定休、昼12:00 (最終入店) 15時クローズ、夜18:00 (最終入店) 22時クローズ。加熱の哲学: 素材にストレスを与えず心地よい温度帯で加熱。食べログ: フレンチ、完全予約制、8席、アレルギー・ベジタリアン・ヴィーガンは事前に相談 (当日の変更は不可)、2021年3月18日オープン、フレンチ WEST 百名店 2023・2025。口コミ (2024〜2026年、英語): 五味のアペリティフ、卵の小宇宙、Kasumi の蟹、京都の茸のスープ、Kyoto Hime beef の低温焼き、ハーブティー。

positives.text: Vegetarian and vegan menus can be arranged on request (official site); vegetarian, vegan and allergy requests must be made in advance — no changes on the day (Tabelog).

kyoto_okakita.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat udon, soba of unstated buckwheat ratio, tempura, curry sauce and nama-fu (wheat gluten), all in a dashi-based broth (official menu; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_okakita.vegan_detail: Not vegan: every bowl sits in dashi — the official site names natural Rishiri kombu, and a May 2026 reviewer tasted kombu and bonito; toppings include chicken, beef, egg, shrimp and herring (official site; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_okakita.hours_raw: 11:00–19:00 (last order 19:00), Monday and Thursday to Sunday; closed Tuesday and Wednesday (official site; Tabelog). No reservations (Tabelog). Expect a queue: 15 people and a 20-minute wait at 13:00 on a holiday Saturday, about 40 minutes on a weekday, five groups ahead 30 minutes before opening (October 2026); a line before 15:00 on a Sunday was gone by 16:30 (November 2026). Staff take orders while you wait, food comes quickly, and diners are expected to finish promptly for the next in line (October 2026). 36 seats; non-smoking; cash only (Tabelog). Children welcome, with child-sized bowls and forks (Tabelog). City bus 5 to the Zoo stop, 2 min north; or 10 min walk from Higashiyama Stn; park in the municipal lot in front for a discount coupon (official site; Tabelog).
kyoto_okakita.notes: [Udon & soba · Okazaki, Kyoto udon by the zoo] A Kyoto udon house in Okazaki, open since 1940, a few minutes from Heian Shrine and the zoo. The kitchen builds its dashi on natural Rishiri kombu, and the thin, soft Kyoto udon is boiled 10–15 minutes; toppings include fried tofu fried by hand every morning at a local tofu shop and nama-fu from 京麩 半兵衛. The tempura udon — big shrimp, a fluffy egg-thickened broth — and the dashi curry udon are what most reviewers order; any bowl can be had with soba instead. Lines are the rule (20–40 minutes in October 2026); staff take orders in the queue and seat you fast. Cash only. 11:00–19:00, closed Tuesday and Wednesday.

roles: The second generation (official site: 二代目) carries on the founder’s dashi; no one is named in the sources
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: founded in Showa 15 (1940); the founder learned the dashi technique in seventeen years of training, and the second generation has refined it over more than fifty years. Ingredients named on the site: buckwheat flour from the foot of 白山 in Ishikawa, organic rice, nama-fu from 京麩 半兵衛, fresh yuba, domestic wagyu and young chicken, wild shrimp, fried tofu fried by hand each morning at a local tofu shop, and Kyoto vegetables. The interior has wooden chairs made by craftsmen and karakami paper with an autumn-grass pattern printed from woodblocks in use since the Edo period. Renewal opened on 20 August 2008 (Tabelog). Tabelog Udon "Tabelog 100" 2017–2019 and Udon WEST 2020, 2024.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: "dashi is the life of Kyoto udon"; to serve a gentle, warm bowl, boiling thin noodles 10–15 minutes while "checking their mood" so they come out glossy with some bite.
chef_bio.specialty: Tempura udon; curry udon; kitsune.

anecdotes.text: A May 2026 regular noted many foreign visitors, who tended to linger after eating, lengthening the wait outside.
An October 2026 diner gave an order while still in the queue and had the food almost as soon as being seated.
"The staff was attentive, frequently checking on us and taking orders while we waited" — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (kyoto-okakita.com): 京うどん 生蕎麦 岡北、創業昭和15年、石川県白山山麓産のそば粉、有機米、京麩 半兵衛さんの生麩、生湯葉、国産和牛、若鶏、天然海老、毎朝手揚げの地元豆腐店のおあげさん、京野菜、出汁は天然利尻昆布のみを使用、初代が十七年の修行で修得した技法を二代目が五十年余りで培った技で仕上げる、細めの麺を10分から15分ゆがく、職人手製の木製椅子、江戸時代からの版木で刷った秋草模様の唐紙、左京区岡崎南御所町34、市バス「動物園前」から北へ徒歩2分、11:00〜19:00 (L.O.)、毎週火曜日・水曜日定休。おしながき: きつね970円、しっぽく1,400円、鳥なんば1,280円、にしんそば1,500円、天ぷらそば1,680円、鍋焼きうどん1,850円、親子なんば1,430円、天とじ1,780円、たぬき1,100円、のっぺい1,450円、生湯葉けいらん1,680円、甘ぎつねカレー1,180円、鳥なんばカレー1,400円、肉カレー1,950円、せいろ980円、天せいろ2,200円 (うどんか蕎麦を選べる)、丼もの: 玉子丼1,000円〜天丼2,000円 (生湯葉入赤だし付き)。食べログ: うどん・そば・丼、予約不可、36席、カード・電子マネー・QR 不可、禁煙、子供用の器とフォーク、2008年8月20日リニューアルオープン、うどん百名店 2017〜2019、うどん WEST 百名店 2020・2024。口コミ (2026年5〜11月、英語): 行列 (20〜40分)、並んでいる間に注文、天ぷらうどん1,680円、カレーうどん、肉うどん1,850円、カレーは辛口と甘口。

kyoto_otabicho_tagoto.gf_detail: Ask when booking. The operator lists gluten-free, vegan and vegetarian options on Tabelog, and the English page says dietary restrictions and food allergies can be accommodated; but this is Kyoto cuisine built on broth and seasonings, and no gluten-free dish is named (Tabelog; official site).
kyoto_otabicho_tagoto.vegan_detail: Ask in advance. The English page says vegetarian or vegan meals can be provided if the shop is told ahead, and notes that the broth for most dishes is made with bonito; the standard bento, yuba and kaiseki menus include fish (official site; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_otabicho_tagoto.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–15:00; dinner 17:00–21:00 (last order 20:00); closed Wednesday and the second Thursday (open on public holidays) (official site; Tabelog). Bookings by phone (toll-free 0120-307-361) or online; a 2-hour stay for lunch and dinner; seat requests (window, quiet room) cannot be taken; changes on the day by phone only (Tabelog). Dishes are decided at booking to cut food waste (Tabelog). The third-floor rooms take only kaiseki of ¥11,000 or more, with a room charge; a service charge applies at lunch and dinner (official site). 108 seats over three floors: tables, sunken kotatsu seats and tatami rooms, up to 32 in the hall; elevator; wheelchair accessible; non-smoking; cards, e-money and QR payments; English menu (Tabelog). 1 min from Hankyu Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn exit 6; partner parking at フヤ町パーキング, 2 hours free for groups spending ¥6,000 or more (official site).
kyoto_otabicho_tagoto.notes: [Kyoto cuisine · Shijo Kawaramachi, a house from 1871] A Kyoto-cuisine restaurant founded in 1871, now in its fifth generation (堀部素久, per the company site) and on Shijo Otabi-cho since moving here from Shinkyogoku after the war. Behind the noren: tables and kotatsu seats downstairs, private rooms and a hall above, a small courtyard garden. The house dish is the Kōetsu mizusashi bento (from ¥4,950), with a yuba course and kaiseki from ¥11,000; English menu, and vegan meals if asked ahead. Lunch 11:30–15:00, dinner to 21:00; closed Wednesday and the second Thursday.

roles: Fifth-generation head of the house and representative director of 株式会社田ごと (company site); the kitchen staff are not named
chef_bio.background: Per the company history page: founded in 1871 (Meiji 4) by 堀部徳兵衛; the second generation renamed the shop from 田毎 to 田ごと in 1938; in 1945, after the war, the shop moved from Shinkyogoku to Shijo Otabi-cho, where it still runs as the Shijo honten; 株式会社田ごと was set up in 1950; the Keio department store shop in Shinjuku opened in 1964; the honten was rebuilt and reopened in 2008; Kyoto Prefecture "Kyoto shinise" award 2013; listed as a provider of seasonal Kyoto vegetables 2014. Today the company runs the Shijo honten, the Shinjuku Keio shop, the Kyoto Takashimaya shop and the Kyoto Porta shop (soba), and sells Kyoto bento at Kyoto Isetan and in Kyoto Station.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: to bring out the best of Kyoto vegetables and nature’s ingredients, express the turning seasons, and give the menu life through a Kyoto sense of beauty. Per Tabelog (operator text): "Cherishing a Simple and Pure Heart."
chef_bio.specialty: Kōetsu mizusashi bento; yuba course; Kyoto kaiseki.

anecdotes.text: "Nearly 40 years ago, I had my first taste of yuba at this restaurant during a family trip to Kyoto." The reviewer came back for a yuba course and chilled sake — August 2026.
A solo diner, put off by the "somewhat intimidating entrance", found staff who said dining alone was fine and seated the reviewer away from larger groups; yuba course ¥5,170 — July 2026.
Lunch kaiseki ¥6,600 with hamo sashimi and Kamo eggplant dengaku, finishing with matcha shaved ice; the reviewer usually eats at the Takashimaya branch across the street — July 2026.
An April 2026 visitor noted many elderly diners and international visitors, Wi-Fi, a courtyard and staff in traditional dress; Kōetsu mizusashi bento ¥4,840.
A September 2026 lunch guest praised the garden-view room but found the wait after the hassun long and the service "somewhat clumsy".

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (kyoto-tagoto.co.jp): 京料理 御旅町田ごと、下京区四条通寺町東入御旅町34番地、阪急河原町駅6番出口から東へ約10メートル、ご昼食11:30〜15:00、ご夕食17:00〜21:00 (L.O20:00)、定休日 水曜日・第2木曜日 (祝日を除く)、霜月の光悦水指弁当 (鯛かぶら鍋とお造り付) 税込7,700円、光悦水指弁当 税込4,950円〜、ゆば料理 税込4,950円〜、お昼の会席 税込7,700円、会席「うさぎ」11,000円・「杵」13,200円・「臼」16,500円・「鶴」22,000円 (税込、飲み物・サービス料別)、3階のお座敷は11,000円以上の会席で別途お部屋代。歴史: 明治4年 (1871年) 初代 堀部徳兵衛、昭和13年「田毎」から田ごとに改名、昭和20年 新京極から四条御旅町に移転、昭和25年 株式会社田ごと設立、昭和39年 新宿京王百貨店に「田ごと光悦舗」、平成20年 本店新装開店、平成25年 京都老舗表彰、五代目 堀部素久 (代表取締役)、現在は四条本店・新宿京王店・京都高島屋店・京都ポルタ店。英語ページ: ベジタリアン・ヴィーガン料理は事前連絡で対応、ほとんどの料理の出汁は鰹。食べログ: 京料理、108席、個室あり、カード・電子マネー・QR 可、英語メニュー、英語・中国語のスタッフ、ヴィーガン・ベジタリアン・グルテンフリーのオプション (店舗情報)。口コミ (2026年1〜9月、英語): ゆば料理、光悦水指弁当、昼の会席、天ぷらそば、かぶら蒸し。

Please note that the broth used for most of our dishes is made with bonito (fish)." It also says vegetarian or vegan meals can be provided with advance notice.

kyoto_salad_sancho_kawaramachi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: the grills are fried shrimp, chicken and beef cutlets, minced cutlets, crab-cream croquettes and teriyaki steak, served with rice or a roll; no gluten information (official menu).
kyoto_salad_sancho_kawaramachi.vegan_detail: Ask. Every grill is meat, seafood or egg; the green salad (six vegetables, house dressing ¥750) and the fresh fruit juices are the plant-based items, but the dressing ingredients are not published, and reviewers mention a homemade mayonnaise (official menu; April 2026).
kyoto_salad_sancho_kawaramachi.hours_raw: 11:30–22:00 (last order 21:00), basically closed 15:30–17:00; lunch menu 11:30–15:30 (official site). Closed Wednesday, plus two extra closing days a month, mostly Tuesdays; the 2026 calendar lists 10 and 24 November, 8 and 22 December, and 30 December–6 January (official site). No bookings; queues of 30 minutes to over an hour are usual, and a reviewer advises joining by about 14:45 for lunch (2026 reviews). Takeaway grills, salads and dressings; dressings ship nationwide (official site). 20 seats (8 counter, 12 table); non-smoking; cash only (Tabelog). 50 m north of Shijo-Kawaramachi, beside Mizuho Bank (Tabelog).
kyoto_salad_sancho_kawaramachi.notes: [Yoshoku · Shijo-Kawaramachi, salads and teriyaki steak since 1972] A small white-walled western-style diner off Shijo that opened in 1972 as a salad specialist: every grill — teriyaki steak, hamburg steak, crab-cream croquettes, fried shrimp — comes with a big, crisp six-vegetable salad in the house dressing, and the lunch sets add rice or a roll and a fresh fruit juice. Weekday lunch from ¥1,200; teriyaki steak with salad ¥1,880. Twenty seats and no bookings, so expect a queue. Cash only; closed Wednesday and two other days a month.

roles: Owner (unnamed; the site carries an "owner diary"); run by サンチョ株式会社
chef_bio.background: Per the shop history page: opened in 1972 (Showa 47) as a salad specialist at the present Kawaramachi honten, as an individual business; became サンチョ株式会社 in 1975; opened a Fushimi branch in 1980 and later other branches; featured in non-no (1979) and other magazines; from 1991 grew its own organic rice and from 1994 bought direct from organic farmers. Today the site lists two shops, the Kawaramachi honten and Fushimi. The company marked its 54th year in September 2026 (owner diary).
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: carefully chosen fresh vegetables and additive-free ingredients, to serve food that is as kind to the body and as tasty as possible; the crispness of the salad unchanged since 1972.
chef_bio.specialty: Green salad with house dressing; teriyaki steak; lunch sets with fresh juice.

anecdotes.text: "I've been a fan of this gem since a friend took me here over 30 years ago." — August 2026.
An August 2026 visitor advised lining up by about 14:45 for lunch, as a first-round miss can mean an hour in the sun, and wished the shop handed out tickets; the staff were friendly and cheerful.
B lunch ¥1,600 after a wait of about 1 hour 10 minutes from before noon — September 2026.
On the weekday lunch, skipping the salad takes ¥200 off; the reviewer kept it — September 2026.
Juice was being made from freshly cut fruit, a diner saw — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (sancho.co.jp): 1972年にサラダの専門店としてオープン、厳選した新鮮な野菜と添加物を使用していない素材、6種類の野菜のグリーンサラダと自家製ドレッシングを全てのグリルに、約18種のサラダ、河原町店 11:30〜22:00 (21:00ラストオーダー、15:30〜17:00は基本的にクローズ)、水曜定休・月2回は連休、中京区裏寺町通四条上ル中之町572。平日ランチ: オムコロランチ1,200円、照り玉バーグランチ1,250円、フライランチ1,300円、テリコロランチ1,480円、ミックスランチ1,230円、ミニジュースセット+150円。土日ランチ (本日の生ジュース付き): Aランチ1,400円、Bランチ1,600円、Cランチ1,880円。照焼ステーキとサラダ1,880円、手作りハンバーグとサラダ1,330円、デミグラスハンバーグとサラダ1,560円、セレクトセット2,880円、グリーンサラダ750円、自家製ドレッシング各650円 (税込)。2026年5月1日から照焼用牛肉とワインの価格改定。2026年の臨時休業日 (11月10日・24日、12月8日・22日、12月30日〜1月6日)。サンチョの歩み: 昭和47年 個人の店として開店、昭和50年 サンチョ株式会社、昭和55年 伏見支店。食べログ: 洋食・ハンバーグ・ステーキ、20席 (カウンター8、テーブル12)、予約不可、カード・電子マネー・QR 不可、禁煙。口コミ (2026年4〜10月、英語): 行列30分〜1時間超、照焼ステーキ、生ジュース、サラダ。

cultural_comfort.note: Queue outside (no bookings); a counter suits solo diners; cash only.

kyoto_mash_kyoto.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a wheat bakery — baguettes, pain de mie, croissants, filled buns and sandwiches (official site; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_mash_kyoto.vegan_detail: Ask. Many breads carry cream, cheese, bacon or egg; plain loaves such as the long-fermented baguette may suit, but no ingredient list is published (official site; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_mash_kyoto.hours_raw: 8:00–19:30, Monday and Thursday to Sunday; closed Tuesday and Wednesday (Tabelog; official site). Closes when sold out (2023 article); reviewers in September–October 2026 found most shelves empty by 9:30–11:00, so go early. Takeaway only, with no café corner or eat-in (Tabelog); the shop’s own site, last updated in 2017, still lists a second-floor café, Cafe 8 huit. Cards accepted (Tabelog). East of Karasuma on Takatsuji-dori, just south of the corner by the Nikko Princess hotel; 4 min from Shijo Stn (Tabelog; 2023 article). Narrow street: no stopping by car (Tabelog).
kyoto_mash_kyoto.notes: [Bakery · Karasuma-Takatsuji, breads like Kyoto sweets] A bakery in a renovated old house near Karasuma-Takatsuji, opened in 2004 by the owner-baker 増野, who trained in Paris before coming home to Kyoto. It is known for buns made to look like wagashi: the green matcha anpan 藤壷 (Fujitsubo), the purple-potato 花のいろは。 with a violet on top, and the jam-and-custard 六条御息所 — plus a long-fermented baguette and generous croissants (¥280). Most shelves are empty by mid-morning. Takeaway only; cards accepted; closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Bread WEST Tabelog 100, 2020, 2022 and 2026.

roles: Owner-baker (ルルブ article, updated July 2023)
chef_bio.origin: Kyoto (the article says the shop opened in the owner's home town).
chef_bio.background: Per a ルルブ article (updated 29 July 2023): the owner-baker found the fun of bread at a Japanese bakery, decided to become a baker, went to Paris to train because "if I aim for it, I have to know the real thing", and after training opened the shop in home-town Kyoto; the building is a renovated old house. Opened 25 March 2004 (Tabelog). Tabelog Bread WEST "Tabelog 100" 2020, 2022, 2026.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: "パンを探究する毎日" — every day spent exploring bread; per the 2023 article, the owner wanted to make "interesting breads that feel like Kyoto".
chef_bio.specialty: 藤壷 (Fujitsubo) matcha anpan; 花のいろは。; long-fermented baguette.

anecdotes.text: Arriving around 11:00, a September 2026 reviewer found about 80% sold out; the Fujitsubo had no noticeable matcha flavour, though the red bean filling was tasty, and the bread itself was "just average in both texture and flavor".
"I was surprised by the size of the croissant." At ¥280 it was "a great price" — September 2026.
A lemon cream sweet came wrapped in bamboo leaves, "making a striking presentation" — October 2026.
At 9:30 most items were sold out; the Kujo-negi and bacon bake and a croque monsieur were being finished in the back — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (mashkyoto.com、2017年まで更新): ブランジュリーまっしゅ京都、京都四条烏丸近く東洞院高辻、8:00am〜7:30pm、火・水曜定休、2F「Cafe 8 huit」(12:00〜18:30頃)、長時間低温熟成発酵のフランスパン (バゲット、エピ、ブール)、塩糀種の小物フランス、京菓子パン: 紫芋のあんぱん「花のいろは。」、抹茶のあんぱん「藤壷-fujitsubo」、桜型のメロンパン。ルルブ (2023年7月29日更新): オーナー兼ブーランジェの増野さん、日本のベーカリーでパンのおもしろさに触れ、フランス・パリで修行、地元の京都で開店、古民家を改築した建物、「京都らしい、おもしろいパンを作りたい」、花のいろは299円、粽あんぱん275円、藤壺297円、六条御息所297円 (ブラックココアの生地にいちごジャム・ラズベリージャム・カスタードクリーム)、にぬき318円、売り切れ次第終了。食べログ: パン・サンドイッチ・スイーツ、下京区東洞院通高辻下る燈籠町568、月・木〜日 8:00〜19:30、火・水休み、テイクアウトのみ (イートインなし)、カード可、2004年3月25日オープン、パン WEST 百名店 2020・2022・2026。口コミ (2026年9〜10月、英語): 早い時間に売り切れ、藤壷410円、クロワッサン280円、食パン290円、タンドリーチキン370円、塩糀ベーコン290円。

cultural_comfort.note: Self-serve bakery; point and pay at the counter; cards accepted.

kyoto_reine_des_pres.gf_detail: Ask when booking. A single omakase course with bread (ciabatta, baguette), pastry desserts and butter or wine sauces; the shop asks guests to state allergies and disliked ingredients in advance and cannot change the menu on the day (Tabelog; 2025–26 reviews).
kyoto_reine_des_pres.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the omakase course is built on fish, shellfish, meat, foie gras, consommé and egg, and the menu is not changed on the day (Tabelog; 2025–26 reviews).
kyoto_reine_des_pres.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30 (last entry 12:00); dinner 18:00 (last entry 19:00); Tabelog gives 11:30–15:00 and 18:00–23:00. Closed Wednesday and the second and third Thursday (may vary); summer break 16–22 August 2026 (official site; Tabelog). Reservation only, by phone, at least two days ahead (same day sometimes possible); 100% cancellation charge from three days before; overseas guests book through Pocket Concierge (official site). Allergies and dislikes must be told in advance (Tabelog). Lunch course ¥11,000, dinner ¥22,000, plus 10% service; wine pairing ¥10,000 (tasting) or ¥16,000 (standard) (official site). Dress code: smart casual, no shorts, short trousers or beach sandals; children from middle-school age, younger only for private bookings (official site; Tabelog). 6 seats; private hire for about 8; non-smoking; cards accepted (official site; Tabelog). 3 min walk from Jingu-Marutamachi Stn (official site).
kyoto_reine_des_pres.notes: [French · Marutamachi, six seats and three ingredients a plate] A six-seat French restaurant on a quiet street near Jingu-Marutamachi, opened in 2012, with wood and stone like a chef's home and dishes on Kiyomizu-ware made with the artists. Only an omakase course: ingredients picked from producers, gently cooked at low temperature, no more than three on a plate — the egg 'Homage to the Master' with maple syrup, a tomato consommé drunk from a matcha bowl, venison with foie-gras-stuffed Manganji pepper. Lunch ¥11,000, dinner ¥22,000 (+10%). Book by phone two days ahead (overseas guests via Pocket Concierge); smart casual. Closed Wednesday and the second and third Thursday.

roles: Chef ("Chef Akai" in a February 2026 review); sommelier-qualified (official site)
chef_bio.background: Opened 26 November 2012 (Tabelog). Per the operator’s Tabelog text: 13 consecutive years in the Michelin Guide and 7 in Gault & Millau; Tabelog French WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025. Per the official site: the chef visits producers, buys directly, and works with ceramic artists on one-of-a-kind dishes; suppliers named in 2026 news include 桃里庵 peaches from Okayama, asparagus from ジェットファーム長谷川 and あいち鴨 duck from Toyohashi; in October 2026 the restaurant held its first curry event at じんぐうみち, an event space by Heian Shrine.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: "素材 × 火入れ × シンプル" — share the vegetables and ingredients producers have raised with care, cook them with the heat the chef has in mind, and finish them as simply as possible with a sense of the season. Per the Michelin Guide: no more than three ingredients on a plate, so a diner can tell what is on the plate.
chef_bio.specialty: Omakase course; 師へのオマージュ egg; tomato consommé.

anecdotes.text: The chef came to the table to explain an approach of blending the essence of Japanese cuisine with French technique, for "depth" beyond immediate deliciousness — January 2026.
For tea, six test tubes were set out to smell before choosing — January 2026.
"Served in a matcha bowl, you drink it just like enjoying a cup of matcha." (the tomato consommé) — September 2026; the same reviewer found the drink menu "a bit too small to read".
A solo lunch guest talked with the serving staff about the tableware and Kyoto — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (reine-des-pres.com): 素材はすべて自ら選びとった上質なもの、仕上げは極上のシンプル、おまかせコースのみ、ランチ11,000円・ディナー22,000円 (税込、サービス料10%別)、ワインペアリング デギュスタシオン10,000円・スタンダード16,000円、ソムリエの資格を持つシェフ、コンセプト「素材×火入れ×シンプル」、作家さんと唯一無二の器、予約は電話 (075-223-2337)、2日前完全予約制、キャンセルは3日前から100%、ドレスコード (短パン、ふくらはぎより短いパンツ、ビーチサンダル等は不可)、上京区中町通丸太町下ル駒之町537-1、京阪神宮丸太町から徒歩3分、ランチ11:30〜12:00 (L.O)、ディナー18:00〜19:00 (L.O)、水曜・第2第3木曜休み (変動あり)、6席、貸切8人、海外の方は Pocket Concierge から予約、お知らせ: 8月16〜22日夏季休暇、岡山 桃里庵の桃、ジェットファーム長谷川の夏アスパラ、あいち鴨、じんぐうみちでのカレーイベント。ミシュランガイド: シェフのテーマは素材、火入れ、シンプル、一皿の食材は三つまで、清水焼の器。食べログ: フレンチ・創作料理・イノベーティブ、予約のみ、6席、カード可、サービス料10%、2012年11月26日オープン、フレンチ WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025、アレルギーと苦手な食材は事前に、中学生以上。口コミ (2025年10月〜2026年9月、英語): トマトのコンソメ、師へのオマージュ、遊びゴコロ、プレミアムかぼちゃ、ジビエ、試験管のお茶、Akai シェフ。

cultural_comfort.note: Book by phone two days ahead, or via Pocket Concierge from overseas; tell allergies when booking; smart casual.

kyoto_ekaki.gf_detail: Ask. The menu mixes fritters, fries, spring-roll sausages, quiche, gratin, toast and pasta with salads, cheeses, charcuterie and grilled meat; no gluten information (official menu).
kyoto_ekaki.vegan_detail: Ask. A few vegetable plates (salted boiled peanuts, black edamame pickles, salads, fritters, fries with black shichimi) sit among meat, cheese and egg dishes; dishes are cooked to the size of the group, so ask (official menu; March 2026).
kyoto_ekaki.hours_raw: 12:00–22:00 daily (Tabelog), but hours vary: the official site posts the day’s hours (4 November: 15:00–22:00, for drinkers only), and a reviewer advises checking Instagram (April 2026). Tabelog says reservations are taken and the site gives a phone number for same-day bookings and changes, yet an April 2026 reviewer called it "a popular restaurant that doesn’t take reservations". House rules (official site): order at least 2 drinks a person (the menu says 2 to 10); dishes are cooked to the size of the group; seats are limited to 2 hours when busy; one cook makes almost everything, so food takes time; when very busy, guests wanting only drinks may be turned away. The menu has no prices (November 2025; April 2026). Japanese menu only, and staff mostly speak Japanese (official site, in English); wines explained via mobile ordering (January 2026). Cards (JCB per Tabelog; contactless per the site), no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 20 seats on two floors with a counter, and benches outside (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Red door, a short alley off the main street; 2 min walk from Kawaramachi Stn (Hankyu) (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews). Opened 20 May 2015 (Tabelog).
kyoto_ekaki.notes: [Izakaya · Kawaramachi, natural wine behind a red door] A small two-floor bistro-izakaya with a red front and benches outside, a short alley off Kawaramachi, open from midday: natural wines chosen to your taste, and plates cooked by one chef who studied natural wine and French cuisine — flap steak, dashi omelette, raisin butter, beet salads, mussels, a chestnut soup in autumn. Portions are big and scaled to the group; order at least two drinks each; the menu has no prices, and reviewers paid about ¥2,000–10,000 a head. Japanese menu only — the shop asks you to try ordering in Japanese. Hours change day to day; check the site or Instagram.

roles: Chef (unnamed), who cooks almost everything alone (official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site (in English): "We’re an izakaya, not a bar"; the chef studied natural wine and French cuisine; one chef makes almost everything. The site lists a sister shop 200 m away, chichi (croissant soft-serve, wine and a gallery space), and sells ekaki goods (stickers, plates, glasses, a logo long-tee). Opened 20 May 2015 (Tabelog). An April 2026 reviewer heard that the owner is sometimes in and sometimes not, which can change the menu; on the second visit the beef steak was not available.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: "let’s enjoy good food, good drinks, and a good time together!"
chef_bio.specialty: Beef flap steak; dashi omelette; raisin butter.

anecdotes.text: "I had some concerns, such as the lack of prices on the menu and the two-drink minimum per person, but in the end, it was an amazing experience!" — November 2025.
"The selection of natural wines was truly impressive, and they made perfect suggestions based on my specific requests." — December 2025.
"I was particularly impressed by the chestnut soup I had at the end! The soup was topped with cocoa" — October 2025.
"The service wasn’t cold, but rather dry with a comfortable distance." The same reviewer noted "Allergy accommodations: Yes". — April 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (ekaki-kyoto.crayonsite.info): その日の営業時間を掲載 (11/4 15:00〜22:00 お酒飲まれる方のみ)、御注文は口頭、人数に合わせて料理、お酒一人2杯〜10杯、お会計はお席で、クレジットカードタッチ決済可、混雑時お席2時間制、1人で料理を作っております、メニュー: グラスワイン・ボトルワイン、生ビール サッポロ、ぶどうビール、日本酒 (奈良・島根・鳥取ほか)、カルダモン焼酎、生搾り酎ハイ、季の美、大人プリン、塩ゆで落花生、アンチョビウフマヨ、焼き芋とカルダモンのポタージュ、いちぢくとブッラータチーズ、サラダリヨネーズ、丹波栗の素揚げ、フライドポテト (黒七味)、ムール貝の白ワイン蒸し、海老とほうれん草のキッシュ、イカのオイルパスタ ブジアーテ、ハチノスとひよこ豆のトマト煮、豚スペアリブのバルサミコ煮、鴨胸ロースト、牛カイノミステーキ、クロックムッシュ (16:00迄)、レーズンバター、出汁オムレツ、当日予約や変更は電話で、系列店 chichi (200mの所、クロワッサンコーン ソフトクリーム、ワイン)。英語の案内: 日本語のメニューのみ、スタッフは主に日本語、シェフは自然派ワインとフランス料理を学んだ。食べログ: ビストロ・バー、下京区貞安前之町611-3、阪急河原町駅から徒歩2分、毎日12:00〜22:00、予約可、20席、カード可 (JCB)、2015年5月20日オープン。口コミ (2025年10月〜2026年4月、英語): 値段のないメニュー、2杯以上の注文、自然派ワイン、ハラミステーキ、出汁オムレツ、レーズンバター、栗のスープ、赤い扉、2階席、外のベンチ。

cultural_comfort.note: Japanese menu only, staff mostly speak Japanese, and the shop asks guests to try ordering in Japanese (official site). At least 2 drinks each.

existence.note: Official site (posting the 4 November hours) and Tabelog listing; reviews dated through April 2026.

kyoto_kyogoku_stand.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: much of the menu is breaded and fried (croquettes, tonkatsu, mixed fry, aji fry, eel tempura), with ramen, fried noodles, curries and shumai (official menu; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_kyogoku_stand.vegan_detail: Not vegan: oden and simmered dishes in dashi, fried meat and fish, and set meals with miso soup; Tabelog lists vegetarian options, but nothing is marked vegan (official menu; Tabelog).
kyoto_kyogoku_stand.hours_raw: 12:00–21:00; closed Tuesday (official site; Tabelog). No reservations (Tabelog); tables are shared, and a seat at the counter is usually found for one (2026 reviews). Except with set meals, each person orders at least one drink and one dish (September and October 2026). A red slip is left on the table and taken to the register, where the bill is added up on an abacus (2026 reviews). Cash only; smoking allowed, and tobacco is sold inside (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). English menu available (Tabelog). 42 seats: a 20-seat counter, three tables for six and one for four (Tabelog). On Shinkyogoku just north of Shijo, near Nishiki Tenmangu; a short walk from Kawaramachi Stn exit 9 (Tabelog; August 2026).
kyoto_kyogoku_stand.notes: [Izakaya · Shinkyogoku, a 1927 tavern with an abacus at the till] A real Showa-era taishu sakaba on the Shinkyogoku arcade, opened in 1927 by a founder who had come from Asakusa after the Great Kanto Earthquake, as a 'ten-sen shokudo' where everything cost ten sen. The marble counter and tables are the originals. Drink from noon at the counter or share a long table: Kirin draft, Gekkeikan sake, homemade croquettes (¥800), kizushi, oden, aji fry. A red slip goes to the register, where the bill is added on an abacus. Cash only; smoking allowed; at least one drink and one dish each. Closed Tuesday. One long-time customer found the food rushed and a server loud in October 2026, but keeps coming for the building and the atmosphere.

roles: Owner at the register (unnamed in the sources)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: the first owner moved from Asakusa in Tokyo after the Great Kanto Earthquake and opened the shop in 1927 (Showa 2) in a Taisho-era building, as a "ten-sen shokudo" where everything cost ten sen; at first there was also a Stand north shop, and stalls in Yasaka Shrine and Maruyama Park in cherry-blossom season; the marble counter and tables are as they were at the founding, along with an early electric register and early-Showa posters. The site calls it "real Showa retro", not made up. Reviews in 2026 describe the owner at the register adding bills on a five-bead abacus.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: the menu keeps the taste, recipes and work of the founder’s day.
chef_bio.specialty: Homemade croquette; oden; set meals.

anecdotes.text: An October 2026 visitor chatted with the owner about the five-bead abacus at the register; the owner said, "It’s never too late to start."
"The owner was quickly calculating with an abacus, and it came to exactly JPY 3000!" — March 2026.

An October 2026 visitor, a customer since living in Kyoto years ago, found the food rushed, the potato salad supermarket-like and a server loud about the shop’s operations, and comes "for the location, the building, and the atmosphere".
"Outside, there were many foreign tourists, but inside felt purely Japanese, with a nostalgic atmosphere as if time had stopped." — August 2026.

kyoto_fuka_nishiki.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: nama-fu is wheat gluten mixed with glutinous rice flour and steamed, and the fu manju and fu taiyaki are made from it (official site; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_fuka_nishiki.vegan_detail: The fu manju is described as house-made smooth bean paste wrapped in nama-fu (wheat gluten and glutinous rice flour) flavoured with aonori and rolled in a bamboo leaf, with no animal ingredient named; a full ingredient list was not seen, so check (official site).
kyoto_fuka_nishiki.hours_raw: 10:00–17:30; closed Monday, and on the last Sunday of each month from February to August (Tabelog; the official site gives 10:00–17:30, closed Monday). kyoto_fuka_nishiki.notes: [Wagashi · Nishiki Market, fu manju from an old nama-fu maker] The Nishiki Market counter of Fuka, a nama-fu maker that has supplied fresh wheat gluten to the Imperial Palace and to Kyoto ryotei since at least the 1860s. The thing to get is the fu manju its own history says Fuka created: smooth bean paste wrapped in chewy, aonori-green fu and a bamboo leaf (¥330–350), eaten chilled. Small fu taiyaki are baked to order (¥352). Two seats and a counter for eating on the spot, with Ippodo bancha for ¥100. 10:00–17:30, closed Monday.

roles: Owner, the 7th generation (official site; unnamed)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: Fuka has long supplied fu to the Kyoto Imperial Palace; its founding year is unknown because its records burned in the upheavals of the late Edo period, but a pass for entering the palace is dated in the Keio era (1865–68), and the present owner is the 7th generation counted from then. Fuka helped bring nama-fu from plain temple cooking into Kyoto cuisine by delivering it fresh to ryotei every morning, and still works mainly to order for ryotei, making 30–40 kinds a day by hand from pumped groundwater with about 20 craftsmen, all of whom study the tea ceremony. The site says Fuka made the first nama-fu manju, an idea attributed to Emperor Meiji, who liked nama-fu. Tabelog Wagashi WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023 and 2026.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: the family business is "craft, not commerce" — use natural ingredients as far as possible and make by hand everything it can.
chef_bio.specialty: Fu manju; fu taiyaki.

anecdotes.text: A September 2026 reviewer noted that the fu is mixed with aonori and the filling is smooth bean paste of Tanba Dainagon azuki; fu manju and bancha came to ¥490.

kyoto_kansendo_gion.notes: [Wagashi · Gion, an old yokan shop down an alley] A small, Showa-feeling yokan shop hidden in an alley just off Shijo-dori in Gion, founded in 1884 according to reviewers. There is no one at the counter: ring the bell and the owner comes out (one reviewer describes a man in a white chef’s coat and black cap). The famous chestnut steamed yokan, packed with chunks of chestnut and wrapped in bamboo leaf (¥2,000), is seasonal — in September 2026 some visitors bought it and others were told it was not yet being made; there is also a silky mizu yokan, and small chilled steamed yokan (¥350) to eat on a walk. Flavours sell out by late afternoon — phone ahead for the big ones. Several reviewers call the service brusque. Cash only; closed Sunday.
